content: If someone is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. For other cases, contact a poison control center without delay. Residents in the United States can call 1-800-222-1222, while those in Canada can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests, such as kidney function tests, may be required. It is important to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in May 2024. It is important to note that this summary does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Before taking cefdinir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillins, or to other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cephalexin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Cefdinir may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It does not pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as some diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false results. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away.
